claims.text: What the image looks like Spiculated solid pulmonary nodule >8 mm, upper lobe → lung cancer (adenocarcinoma if peripheral)
claims.quote: Spiculated solid pulmonary nodule >8 mm, upper lobe Lung cancer (adenocarcinoma if peripheral)

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Lung fields: symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules
claims.quote: F - Fields (lung): symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules.
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy → ABCDE-FGHI)

claims.text: Solitary pulmonary nodule: a discrete lesion < 3 cm, completely surrounded by lung parenchyma, without atelectasis or pleural effusion
claims.quote: A solitary pulmonary nodule is a discrete lesion < 3 cm in diameter that is completely surrounded by lung parenchyma (ie, does not touch the hilum, mediastinum, or pleura) and is without associated atelectasis or pleural effusion.

claims.text: Spiculated or irregular (scalloped) margins are more indicative of cancer
claims.quote: Margins that are spiculated or irregular (scalloped) are more indicative of cancer.

claims.text: Upper lobe location carries a higher risk of malignancy
claims.quote: Location in the upper lobe carries a higher risk of malignancy.

claims.text: Diameter < 1.5 cm strongly suggests benign; > 5.3 cm strongly suggests cancer (nonmalignant exceptions: lung abscess, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, hydatid cyst)
claims.quote: Diameter< 1.5 cm strongly suggests a benign etiology; diameter > 5.3 cm strongly suggests cancer. However, nonmalignant exceptions include lung abscess, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and hydatid cyst.

claims.text: Calcification suggests nonmalignant disease, particularly central (tuberculoma, histoplasmoma), concentric (healed histoplasmosis) or popcorn (hamartoma)
claims.quote: Calcification suggests nonmalignant disease, particularly if it is central (tuberculoma, histoplasmoma), concentric (healed histoplasmosis), or in a popcorn configuration (hamartoma).

claims.text: Growth: no enlargement in ≥ 2 years suggests benign; volume doubling time 21 to 400 days is likely malignant
claims.quote: A lesion that has not enlarged in ≥ 2 years suggests a benign etiology. Tumors that have volume doubling times from 21 to 400 days are likely to be malignant.

claims.text: Probability of malignancy: less than 1% for all nodules < 6 mm and 1 to 2% for nodules between 6 and 8 mm
claims.quote: it should be noted that the probability of malignancy is less than 1% for all nodules < 6 mm and 1 to 2% for nodules between 6 and 8 mm (1).

claims.text: Causes Lung carcinoma is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide; approximately 85% of cases are related to cigarette smoking
claims.quote: Lung carcinoma is the leading cause of cancer-related death in both men and women worldwide. Approximately 85% of cases are related to cigarette smoking.

claims.text: Adenocarcinoma is the most common subtype of non–small cell lung cancer, especially in people who have never smoked
claims.quote: Histologically, NSCLC is further subclassified into (3): Adenocarcinoma: The most common subtype, especially in people who have never smoked

claims.text: Symptoms Cough, chest discomfort or pain, weight loss and, less commonly, hemoptysis; many patients with early disease and some with metastatic disease have no symptoms at diagnosis
claims.quote: Symptoms can include cough, chest discomfort or pain, weight loss, and, less commonly, hemoptysis. However, many patients with early disease and some with metastatic disease have no symptoms at the time of diagnosis.

claims.text: Can also present with fever, hoarseness, pleural effusion, pneumonia, Pancoast tumor, paraneoplastic syndromes, SVC syndrome, Horner syndrome, and brain, liver or bone metastases
claims.quote: Manifestations can include cough, fever, hoarseness, pleural effusion, pneumonia, Pancoast tumor, paraneoplastic syndromes, superior vena cava syndrome, Horner syndrome, and metastases to the brain, liver, and bone.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: CT, PET, biopsy; Fleischner criteria
Interval imaging is the mainstay for a solitary nodule; the plan depends on size, ground-glass vs semi-solid vs solid, and risk factors (heavy smoking, asbestos, family history, older age)
claims.quote: The mainstay of diagnosis of solitary pulmonary nodules is interval imaging. Specific imaging recommendations depend on the size of the nodule and whether the nodule is ground-glass, semi-solid, or solid, and individual risk factors (history of heavy smoking, exposure to asbestos, family history of lung cancer, older age [1]).

claims.text: PET: sensitivity > 90%, specificity about 78%; SUV > 2.5 suggests cancer; false negatives are more likely if nodules are < 8 mm
claims.quote: It has a sensitivity > 90% and a specificity of about 78% for detecting cancer. PET activity is quantified by the standardized uptake value (SUV) of (18)F-2-deoxy-2-fluoro-D-glucose (FDG). SUV > 2.5 suggests cancer, while nodules with SUV < 2.5 are more likely to be benign. False-negative results are more likely if nodules are < 8 mm.

claims.text: Confirm the diagnosis and staging with cytology or histopathology; resect early-stage NSCLC when pulmonary reserve is adequate
claims.quote: Confirm the diagnosis and staging with cytology or histopathology. Treat early-stage NSCLC with resection when pulmonary reserve is adequate.

claims.text: Screening: annual low-dose CT for people 50 to 80 at high risk (> 20 pack-years; current smokers or quit < 15 years ago), after shared decision making
claims.quote: Recommend annual lung cancer screening with low-dose CT for people who currently smoke and those who formerly smoked who are 50 to 80 years of age and at high risk (> 20 pack-years of smoking, people who are current smokers or who formerly smoked and quit < 15 years ago); shared decision making should occur before imaging is pursued.
